items.title: Natively an argument read through a `Shared` view is copied out of the cell when it is evaluated, so a LATER argument that writes the cell is not seen by the callee — `has(cell.read().items, grow(cell))` and `cell.read().probes.contains(mark(cell))` (a user-hashed key) print `false` natively and `true` on JS, silently
items.body: The JS backend evaluates the receiver/argument to a reference, then the later argument writes through the same cell, then the callee reads the written value. Natively the `read_with(|view| view.items.clone())` copy is taken in argument order, before the writing argument runs. F123 fixed the shape for std's keyed lookups over a std-hashed key (the receiver is a view of the cell borrowed AFTER the key is evaluated, as F114's intrinsics); every other call keeps the early copy. Fix: in the call emission, when an argument reads through a `Shared` view (or a boxed binding) and a later argument may run code, settle the later arguments first (they are hoisted already when `borrows_a_cell`) and take the copy last — the order spec §6.9's native note states for views. Expected on both: `true`, `true`. Sizing S–M; vilan-rust's call seam.

items.title: A closure parameter over the result of a `.map` is not checked against its uses — `let words = ["a", "bb"].map(\|word\| word.len()); words.filter(\|length\| { let probe: str = length; .. })` checks clean (JS runs it; rustc refuses E0308 natively), while an annotated `let words: List<usize>` refuses the `let` "Expected str, but got usize"
items.body: Found while pinning F128: the probe `let probe: str = length` inside `.map(..).filter(|length| ..)` was accepted, so the closure parameter's type is still open when the body is checked and nothing re-checks it once `map`'s `U` settles. The native backend renders the settled `usize` and rustc refuses the program ("a BACKEND defect" by the CLI's sentence) — the checker owes the error. Expected on both: `Expected str, but got usize instead.` at the `let`. Sizing S; the solver (re-check of a closure body after its parameter settles, or fill-from-use B599).
